newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - May 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - May 21.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Wednesday:
* A federal appeals court in Manhattan has ruled that judges have the obligation to make sure jurors do not ignore evidence or law in a case.
* The Federal Reserve voted to hold interest rates steady.
* The U.S. Senate passed a bill that would ban partial-birth abortions, but it failed to garner enough votes to override an expected veto by President Clinton.
* American diplomats have determined that a quarter of the homes in Jewish settlements in the West Bank and half in the Gaza Strip are empty.
* The Clinton administration's plan to pay $1 billion the U.S. owes in dues to the United Nations has stalled in Congress.
* Lawyers for accused Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh attacked the FBI lab's handling of the case.
* President Clinton and former President Jimmy Carter are growing closer after a frosty relationship that marked Clinton's first term in office.
* Four teenagers have been arrested on charges they gang-raped a 14-year-old girl in an unused classroom at a high school in the Queens borough of New York.
